tasks.description: Port compile-dendry.js from Flyt as a runtime-neutral parameterised CLI with its tests: the title fallback, the input and output roots and the one-subgame-per-subdirectory convention become parameters, and the output is byte-identical under Node, Bun and Deno
tasks.notes: Was Flyt 10IC.5. Flyt's ADR 0002 (docs/adr/0002-compiler-home.md on Flyt's main) is the brief and records the evidence. Runtime-neutral means: import built-ins with the node: prefix (node:fs, node:path), sort every directory listing before use, use no API only one runtime has and pin no behaviour to a runtime. Flyt measured the existing script (imports only fs and path) unchanged under Node 25.2.1, Bun 1.3.5 and Deno 2.9.7: all exit cleanly, but Bun lists directories in a different order from Node and the compiler inserts scenes in read order, so great-hall.json has the same 94 scenes in a different order under Bun. Acceptance: a fixture story compiled under all three runtimes with the outputs compared; if CI cannot install all three, record which it covers and which is checked by hand. The CLI lives in src/cli/, outside src/lib. Acceptance includes the engine vocabulary guard covering it, which means widening all three src/lib spots in .github/workflows/engine-vocabulary.yml: the pull_request.paths trigger (line 12), the push.paths trigger (line 17) and the git diff pathspec in the run step (line 48). Widening only the triggers would run the job on a CLI change but still diff src/lib alone, so it would report clean. Also needs its own build step and package.json export, because npm run build is svelte-package -i src/lib -o dist and src/cli is not packaged by it

tasks.description: Keep the compiler CLI behind its own export path so browser bundles never import file system code
tasks.notes: Review note carried from Flyt PR #30. The constraint is file system code out of the browser bundle; the CLI itself stays runtime-neutral (1CC.1). The CLI sits in src/cli/, outside the src/lib tree that svelte-package builds for the browser entry, so it ships through its own build output and export path and nothing in the browser entry imports it

tasks.description: Document how to run the compiler CLI under Node, Bun and Deno
tasks.notes: Split from 1CC.3 because these commands cannot be checked until the CLI ships. The package bin entry carries the usual node shebang because npm expects it; Bun users run it with bunx --bun (the flag is listed by bunx --help on Bun 1.3.5) and Deno users with deno run --allow-read --allow-write (Flyt's invocation, unverified here; Deno is low priority). Re-check every command against the shipped CLI before documenting it
Flyt then bumps the dependency, switches its compile:dendry script to the CLI and retires scripts/compile-dendry.js (Flyt-side tasks)

tasks.description: Document reset() in the README, and decide whether evaluateCondition is public API (a README row) or internal (marked so in the types)
tasks.notes: From Flyt, found while fixing a review comment on Flyt PR #29: Flyt's CLAUDE.md now defers to this README for the engine API. reset() clears the loaded game and state and returns loading and error to their defaults (Flyt calls it when the player returns to the menu); restart() returns to the first scene of the same game, and is the only one the README mentions. The 1.1.0 type declarations also expose evaluateCondition(condition?: string): boolean (src/lib/engine.svelte.ts:797), which the README omits. Changelog entry goes under Unreleased; ship as a 1.1.x patch or fold into the next release
